name: wf-postmortem
description: wf postmortem pack: the postmortem capability, a presence-only feature that owns no provider surface and attaches no phase fragment, so registering it changes no core phase, but its guided skill requires the registration: until /wf-postmortem:init (or /wf:init) registers the pack, the skill's pack-owned references cannot resolve and it stops, writing nothing, pointing at that command. The skill hunts a described failure through prior agent sessions in scope — named explicitly with --session, or located automatically under a resolved scope behind one replaceable seam that owns all host-specific knowledge of the session store, its layout, and the 30-day retention window. The seam stops the hunt only when the store itself is unreadable; an unrecognized record or attached entry is skipped against its own session and named in Coverage instead of aborting the hunt. Every located session is ranked (scope-match specificity, then recency, hunt sessions always last) without ever being silently dropped, and read up to a per-run cap (default 15, overridable with --cap) — every session beyond it is listed skipped (budget), retrievable by a later --report <path> follow-up that reads those sessions and extends the same report file in place. Each session is read by its own isolated reader agent on a cheaper model tier — in ordered windows when a record is too large for one reader — so raw session content never enters the host context; a located session's iterations, edits, and files-touched counts are mechanically observed wherever the seam counts them deterministically. Every reader-suggested mechanism with a locator is then checked two-sided, against the audited pack's own text at its resolved executed version and against a bounded, redacted excerpt fetched fresh at the locator, and promoted to a confirmed contributing factor only when both sides verify. An always-run coverage cross-check then names any in-scope run that left no matching session, and — only when a finding is under-evidenced from sessions alone or left no session record — draws labelled fallback evidence from task folders, delivery history, and other configured sources, never confirming a factor on its own. The report then states a fix direction, apart from the evidence, marked stated or resting on an open choice — or, when no factor was confirmed, marked "— (no confirmed factor)" — and closes with a rule-based recommendation naming the next workflow, first match wins: a terminus only when no factor was confirmed and no hypothesis remains, research when only hypotheses remain — dispatching and filing nothing itself. A hunt whose described failure matches nothing, or whose resolved scope locates no session, still writes a valid report whose finding reads "not found"; that is never a stop. Ships /wf-postmortem:postmortem, the guided skill, plus /wf-postmortem:init for one-command self-registration.
